questions.q: Kaufman's films feature a portal into an actor's head and a company that erases memories. How does that fit his plea to 'say who you are'?
choices: It doesn't: he only means it for memoirists
He means emotional honesty: invented premises can carry the writer's real anxieties
He means writers should only write about real events
He means every script should include the writer as a character
questions.explain: 'Say who you are' is about being honest and vulnerable, not about subject matter, so it's different from 'write what you know'.

questions.q: What did Kaufman tell writers about failure in his 2011 BAFTA lecture?
choices: Avoid it by testing scripts with audiences
It proves you didn't follow the paradigm
It only matters if the film loses money
It's a badge of honour, because it means you took a risk
questions.explain: Kaufman argued that a writer who never risks failure can't make anything new.

questions.q: In Adaptation, what happens after Charlie attends Robert McKee's seminar?
choices: The film's last act turns into the guns, drugs, chase and life lesson he swore off
He abandons the script and returns to television
McKee rewrites the screenplay himself
The film ends with Charlie still blocked and nothing resolved
questions.explain: The final act plays as if Donald, the formula-loving twin, wrote it, making the formula the film's subject.

questions.q: What's the joke in the McKee seminar scene in Adaptation?
choices: McKee warns against voice-over while we're hearing Charlie's voice-over
McKee is played by Charlie Kaufman
McKee recommends the three unities
The seminar is held in a swamp
questions.explain: The film uses the very device McKee condemns, at the moment he condemns it.

questions.q: Why does Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind run through Joel's memories backwards, inside an erasure?
choices: To follow the hero's journey stage by stage
Because the structure carries the question: knowing how it ended, would you do it again?
To disguise a missing second act
To obey the unity of time
questions.explain: Kaufman builds a structure for each story so the form expresses its idea; here, love seen from its ending.

questions.q: A screenwriter wants to follow Kaufman. Which approach is closest to his position?
choices: Pick the beat sheet that best fits the genre
Reject structure entirely
Ask what shape this particular story needs, and build the structure from its idea
Write the ending first and outline backwards to the inciting incident
questions.explain: Kaufman doesn't reject structure; he invents it for each story. His quarrel is with formula used because it sells.

questions.q: Which is the strongest objection to Kaufman's approach?
choices: It can become self-absorbed, and resisting the market is easier for an established writer
It's too dependent on the three-act paradigm
It ignores character entirely
It was designed for journalism, not film
questions.explain: Critics call some of his work solipsistic, and many working writers can't afford to refuse commercial conventions.

ideas: Be honest about who you are, in your life and your work, so your writing might reach someone lost.
Failure is a badge of honour, because it means you took a risk.
A writer who can't adapt a plotless book can put his own block on screen, and let a fictional twin write the formula ending.
Tell a love story from inside the erasure of its memories, newest first.
